newsitem.title: ERITREA: S.Korean firms win Eritrean power plant contract.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean firms win Eritrean power plant contract.

text.p: A South Korean consortium has signed an agreement with the Eritrean government to build a $114 million heavy fuel oil power plant at Hirghigo on the Red Sea coast, Eritrean officials said on Tuesday.

Korea Heavy Industries and Construction Company Ltd. (Hanjung) and Daewoo subsidiary Keangnam beat bids from four rivals for the contract, said Abraham Woldemikael, head of Eritrea's Electric Authority.

He said the Abu Dhabi Fund for Development, Saudi Fund for Development, Kuwait Fund for Arab Economic Development, the Arab Bank for African Economic Development and an Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries development fund had contributed $102 million in loans for the project.
The balance would be met by the government, he said.

Eritrea depends totally on crude oil imports from Saudi Arabia for its power supply, even though recent projects have studied the possibility of exploiting geothermal energy from a dormant volcano in the Denkalia region.
In a joint venture with the Ethiopian government, Eritrea refines 700,000 metric tonnes of crude oil per year, according to the Energy Department of the Ministry of Energy and Mines.
The estimated Eritrean consumption is between 230,000 and 250,000 metric tonnes per year.
